title: Tenant microburst detangler with predictive kernel steering
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Background:
Microbursts from heavy tenants (chatty single-user sessions, aggressive retries, or batched inference clients) create short, high-density prefills that collide with long-running decode-heavy requests. The current allocator favors a single kernel path per request which leads to two problems: 1) kernel mismatch (using long-context kernels for short prefills increases tail latency), and 2) contention hotspots causing tenant unfairness and p95/p99 tail spikes.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a 'microburst detangler' layer in the prefill->decode pipeline that: 1) predicts microburst shape (prefill length, likely decode length, attention cost) from request metadata and recent tenant patterns, 2) splits the request into micro-slices when beneficial, and 3) routes each slice to the kernel variant best matched for its shape (low-overhead short-kernel vs throughput-optimized long-kernel). The system enforces tenant-aware fairness credits during bursts and provides conservative coalescing heuristics to preserve KV cache locality when splitting would harm cache reuse.

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce p95 prefill+first-decode latency for latency-sensitive tenants by >= 15% on mixed workloads.
- Keep overall GPU throughput within -5% of baseline for the evaluated workload mixes.
- Improve worst-case fairness (slowdown ratio of high-traffic tenants vs baseline) by >= 25%.
- No increase in cache-miss rate > 10% post-splitting across observed models.

Design details:
1) Predictor: lightweight on-path model (logistic tree) that uses: tenant rate window, prior request lengths, model profile (seq-len distribution), and client hints (expected response length). Runs in <250us.
2) Splitter: decides micro-slice boundaries with conservative thresholds (min slice 8 tokens, max slices 4), and flags slices "cache-affine" when prefill prefix likely reused by decode.
3) Kernel steering: kernel pool tagged by optimization profile (short-latency-optimized, amortized-throughput, quantized-fastpath). Router picks kernel per slice and emits hints for kernel-selection telemetry.
4) Fairness: tenant credit bucket (moving window) charges tokens for slices; when credits low, splitter falls back to coarser-grained batching or enqueues to dedicated latency capacity.
5) Fallbacks: hedged-fallback to baseline single-kernel path when split increases estimated cost or cache miss risk.

Implementation plan:
Phase A (2 weeks): offline simulation using perf traces (prefill/decode traces from last 30 days). Build predictor and splitter simulator, generate tradeoff matrix for slice sizes vs cache hit.
Phase B (3 weeks): runtime prototype behind feature-flag on canary pool (non-critical region). Components: predictor lib (C++), splitter in scheduler, kernel-router hooks. Add telemetry (per-slice timing, cache-hit, kernel-selection).
Phase C (2 weeks): incremental rollout + ab-test to 10% of traffic, compare metrics and run regressions on evaluation prompts.

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Splitting increases scheduler overhead and KV cache fragmentation; mitigations: cache-affinity heuristics and slice minimum size.
- Predictor false-positives may increase perf variance; we keep conservative thresholds for release.
- Kernel specialization might reduce multiplexing efficiency for rare kernels; monitor utilization and auto-collapse low-util kernels.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary run demonstrates p95 latency improvement >= 12% or clear operator control to disable per-tenant.
- End-to-end testbench shows throughput drop <= 5% on synthetic mixed workload.
- No security-sensitive metadata used in predictor; security signoff obtained if any tenant identifiers are persisted.

Rolling and observability:
- Feature flag: runtime.scheduling.microburst_detangler.
- Dashboards: prefilling/p95_by_tenant, slice_hit_rate, kernel_util_by_tag, tenant_credit_balance.
- Alerts: slice_hit_rate < 75% or kernel_util_spike > 200% of baseline.

Related work and references:
- See experimental sims: https://github.com/redwood-inference/simulations/microburst-detangler (bench results attached)
- Design notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/MBD-Design
